title: Portfolio Limits on a Borrower's Home Mortgage Loans
content:
A customer of Piedmont Crescent Bank may carry several Home Mortgage Loans notes at once. Credit Administration limits how many, both across the whole of the borrower's mortgage holdings and within a single program.

## The limits

1. Before a new application is recorded, the count of the customer's mortgage loans standing in applied, active, delinquent or forbearance status must be below 4.
2. The count for the requested program must also be below that program's own limit on the number of loans of it one borrower may carry.
3. Only one FHA or VA loan may be outstanding at a time for a primary residence.
4. Loans that have been paid off and applications that were withdrawn do not count toward either count.

Both counts are taken from the bank's records of the customer's mortgage loans, correlated to that customer, and are taken before the new application is recorded; what the customer states about how many loans they hold does not decide them.

## The same limits read as a test

| Question | Basis |
|---|---|
| Which loans count? | The customer's mortgage loans standing in applied, active, delinquent or forbearance status |
| Which loans do not count? | Loans paid off, and applications withdrawn |
| How many may stand across all programs? | The count must be below 4 before the new application is recorded |
| How many may stand within the requested program? | The count must be below that program's own limit |
| What is the position on the two agency programs? | Only one FHA or VA loan may be outstanding at a time for a primary residence |

## Points of judgement

Take a hypothetical borrower whose records show two active mortgage loans, one delinquent loan and one loan paid off last year. Three loans stand in a counted status and the paid-off loan does not count, so the across-programs count is 3, which is below 4, and that limit does not stand in the way of a further application. Were all four of those loans standing in a counted status, the count would be 4, which is not below 4.

Take a second hypothetical borrower who holds one FHA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage on a primary residence and applies for a VA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage on a primary residence. Only one FHA or VA loan may be outstanding at a time for a primary residence, so the second of the two is not open to this borrower while the first is outstanding, however low the across-programs count stands.
